name: Amsterdam Neuroscience Meetings and Webinars
note: Annual-meeting sessions and webinars from Amsterdam's neuroscience institute; researchers describe their own work. Not peer-reviewed.

name: Neuroscience and Neurotechnology Seminar Series
note: Monthly SFU seminars on sleep, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, aggression and attention; each speaker presents their own research. Not peer-reviewed.

name: Psychology Grand Rounds
note: Mount Sinai clinical psychology grand rounds on dementia care, OCD, ethics and therapy; clinicians present their own work. Not peer-reviewed.

name: Roybal Center Grand Rounds
note: Columbia grand rounds on PTSD after heart events, fear, pain and heart-brain links; speakers present their own research. Not peer-reviewed.

name: Faith and Neuroscience Colloquium: Perspectives on Personhood
note: Loyola colloquium where theologians, philosophers and neuroscientists discuss personhood, evolution and reductionism; speakers give their own views.

name: Colloquium on Law, Neuroscience, and Criminal Justice (2014)
note: Neuroscientists and legal scholars brief federal judges on brain imaging, juvenile justice, addiction and memory at Vanderbilt in 2014.

name: Colloquium on Law, Neuroscience, and Criminal Justice (2013)
note: Scientists and legal scholars brief judges at Stanford in 2013 on adolescent decision making, violence, addiction and criminal responsibility.

name: Clinical Psychology Colloquium
note: UNC colloquium talks by psychologists on structural racism, identity, adverse childhood experiences and community-based research; speakers' own accounts.

name: Monday Colloquium
note: Max Planck Tübingen colloquium: invited researchers on vision, decision making, olfaction, sleep and brain decoding. Not peer-reviewed.

name: KITP Neuroscience Talks
note: Physicists' seminars and public lectures on the brain, hearing, Alzheimer's and neural networks from the Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics.

name: Transdisciplinary Research Colloquium on Psychedelics
note: Exeter colloquium of 50 talks on psychedelic science, therapy, ethnobotany and philosophy; some speakers advance speculative views. Not peer-reviewed.

name: James Giordano Lectures on Neuroethics
note: James Giordano's lectures on neuroethics, pain, moral sense and the brain-mind-self question; a single speaker's own account.

name: Athena Demertzi: Talks on Consciousness and the Brain
note: Athena Demertzi's talks on the neural basis of consciousness and patients with disorders of consciousness, some in Greek or French.

name: CS 198-96 Intro to Neurotechnology
note: Student-taught Berkeley course (Spring 2020) from macro and micro neuroscience through imaging, clinical applications and neuroethics.

name: Brain Awareness Week 2021
note: IIT Gandhinagar outreach talks on movement, memory, bilingualism, spatial maps and psychosis genetics; researchers describe their own work.

name: Visiting Lecturers on Mind and Brain
note: Mixed talks and interviews from Emory's mind-brain center: moral psychology, mindreading and speech; many clips are short. Not a course.

name: James Giordano Interviews on Neuroscience, Ethics and Science Fiction
note: Short bioethics interviews with James Giordano using films and science fiction to discuss neurotechnology and transhumanism; one speaker's views.

name: Foundations of Neuroimaging (2021)
note: Marty Sereno's course on the physics and math of MRI, fMRI analysis, cortical surface methods, EEG and MEG; math-heavy but pitched slowly.

name: Foundations of Neuroimaging (Updated)
note: Marty Sereno's updated online course on MRI physics, fMRI time series, cortical surface reconstruction, EEG and MEG signals.

name: ILAE-YES Course on Advanced Neuroimaging Techniques in Epilepsy
note: Specialist 2023 course for epilepsy researchers: MRI protocols, FreeSurfer, voxel-based morphometry and detecting focal cortical dysplasia.

name: Lecture Series on Neuroscience
note: IIT Madras talks by invited researchers on reading, motor control, basal ganglia models and Parkinson's; speakers present their own work.

name: TINS Neuroscience Seminar Series
note: Six research seminars on zebrafish emotional states, cortical algorithms, dopamine and psychosis circuits; speakers' own accounts. Not peer-reviewed.

name: Information and Neuroscience
note: NSF center lectures linking information theory and neuroscience: brain-machine interfaces, visual cortex models, brain atlases and blood flow.

name: Columbia Neuroscience Seminars
note: Columbia's weekly invited seminars on dopamine, circuits, cell types and motor control; speakers present their own findings. Not peer-reviewed.

name: Neuroethics Seminar Series 2015-2016
note: MacLean Center seminars on cognitive liberty, deep brain stimulation, brain injury, prosthetics and psychoanalysis; speakers' own views.

name: William K. Warren Jr. Frontiers in Neuroscience
note: Laureate Institute lecture series with leading researchers on mood disorders, psychosis, anorexia, addiction and well-being; speakers' own accounts.

name: McGovern Institute Talks and Events
note: MIT colloquia, prize lectures and symposia, including rare brain disorders; mostly researchers presenting their own work. Not peer-reviewed.

name: Cognitive Science: A Multidisciplinary Introduction
note: Ryan Rhodes's 24-lecture introduction to cognitive science: mind-body problem, computation, Turing machines and linguistic structure.

name: Philosophy of Mind and Cognitive Science Talks
note: Rotman Institute talks by Barrett, Chalmers, Block, Gopnik and others on emotion, perception, memory and consciousness; speakers' own views.

name: 8th Annual Conference of Cognitive Science (ACCS8)
note: Sessions from Amrita's January 2022 cognitive science conference: keynotes, paper and poster sessions. Researchers' own accounts, not peer-reviewed.

name: Nobel Conference 1984: How We Know
note: Six 1984 conference lectures by Milner, Simon, Edelman, Dennett and others on memory, learning and machine thinking. Dated science.

name: The Situated Brain: Culture, Context and Ecologies of Mind
note: McGill's 2023 Advanced Study Institute talks on culture, context and psychiatry's brain research, led by Laurence Kirmayer; speakers' own views.

name: 2022 Beijing Brain Conference
note: Long conference sessions on memory, sleep, neural development, brain-inspired computing, depression imaging and child development. Not peer-reviewed.

name: Philosophy of Deep Learning
note: Debate and conference talks organized by Ned Block, David Chalmers and Raphael Milliere on what deep learning means for cognitive science.

name: Data Science and AI for Neuroscience Summer School 2023
note: Caltech's two-week 2023 summer school on regression, neural population dynamics, encoding models and machine learning for neural data.

name: MIND Summer School 2017
note: Dartmouth's 2017 methods school: lectures and tutorials on fMRI analysis, model fitting, event cognition, memory and connectivity.

name: MIND Summer School 2019
note: Dartmouth's 2019 methods school: coding tutorials (Python, Git, Docker) plus talks on cognitive maps, head direction cells and cortical coding.

name: MIND Summer School 2018
note: Dartmouth's 2018 methods school: tutorials on Git and Jupyter, plus talks on encoding models, timescales of perception and shared memory.

name: NeuroHackademy 2025
note: University of Washington's 2025 neuroimaging and data science summer school: hands-on tools, reproducible analysis, and project presentations.

name: NeuroHackademy 2026
note: University of Washington's 2026 neuroimaging and data science summer school: Python tools, machine-learning biomarkers, and hackathon projects.

name: Ruthazer Lab Talks and Neuro Light Lunch
note: Edward Ruthazer's lab talks and Neuro Light Lunch seminars on imaging brain circuit development in the visual system; some French.

name: Geoffrey Aguirre: fMRI and Neuroscience Lectures
note: Geoffrey Aguirre's fMRI course days and public talks on brain imaging, its hype and its ethics.

name: The Human Sense of Smell
note: April 2017 Columbia panel on how the brain handles smell, with neuroscientists, philosophers and a perfumer; each speaker gives their own view.

name: Lectures by Earl Miller
note: Earl Miller's talks on working memory, brain rhythms and consciousness; one researcher's account, including still-debated claims about waves.

name: Neuroscience and Society Overview
note: Penn talks on neuroethics, fMRI basics, emotion and decision making, and brain-based claims; Farah, Aguirre, Phelps and Satel.

name: Nuffield Department of Clinical Neurosciences Talks
note: Oxford talks, many on sleep and body clocks by Russell Foster, plus gut microbes and phantom limbs; mostly short public lectures.

name: Caltech Researchers on Their Work
note: Caltech public talks and short features on fear, neuroeconomics, brain-machine chips and the fly brain; researchers' own accounts.

name: Monell Seminar Series
note: Monell Center seminars on smell, taste, gut-brain feeding circuits and sensory science; includes some non-neuroscience talks.

name: 3rd HBP School: Future Neuroscience
note: Human Brain Project school lectures on brain atlasing, synaptic mapping, cortical physiology and Blue Brain modelling.

name: Ashley Juavinett Public Talks
note: Neuroscientist Ashley Juavinett on spotting neuro-nonsense, becoming a neuroscientist and open science in teaching.

name: Harvard Brain Science Initiative Lectures and Seminars
note: Harvard talks incl. a '101' series on bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, Alzheimer's, ALS, fear and sleep; speakers' own accounts.

name: Lifelong Brain Development and Brain Ageing
note: Cambridge Neuroscience talks on neurodegeneration, Parkinson's, child mental health, ageing and brain organoids; speakers' own research.

name: CNS6: Noise Models for Neuron Models
note: Gerstner's computational neuroscience module on escape noise, stochastic spike arrival, spike train likelihood and rate versus temporal codes.

name: Zangwill Club Talks
note: Cambridge Zangwill Club talks on time perception, hippocampus, decision making and cognition; speakers present their own work. Not peer-reviewed.

name: CNS3: Synapses, Dendrites and the Cable Equation
note: Gerstner's computational neuroscience module on synapses, short-term plasticity, dendrites as cables and compartmental neuron models.

name: CNS4: Two-Dimensional Neuron Models and Phase Plane Analysis
note: Gerstner's module reducing Hodgkin-Huxley to two dimensions, with phase plane analysis, type I and II neurons and nonlinear integrate-and-fire.

name: CNS8: Fokker-Planck Equation for Integrate-and-Fire Neurons
note: Gerstner's module using the Fokker-Planck equation for neuron populations under stochastic input, ending with the Brunel network.

name: CNS7: Modern Phenomenological Neuron Models
note: Gerstner's module on adaptation and bursting, with AdEx, Spike Response and Generalized Linear models and parameter estimation from data.

name: CNS5: Variability of Spike Trains
note: Gerstner's module on spike train variability: sources of noise, rate codes, Poisson models and membrane potential fluctuations.

name: Brain and Behavior
note: NYU's undergraduate Brain and Behavior course, taught by Wendy Suzuki in 2012: neurons, neurotransmitters, hormones, vision and more, in syllabus order.
